changes.reason: The truncation account predicts persistent sub-10 effective_horizon. In the 8 sampled controller updates it is 10 control intervals at updates 0,5,10,15,20,25 and reduces only at the two latest sampled updates, update 30 (5) and update 34 (1), where the reduction exactly equals the remaining task time (0.05 s -> 5 intervals; 0.01 s -> 1 interval). Persistent budget-driven terminal truncation is therefore not observed; the sampled horizon follows the controller receding to the terminal. Marked weakened rather than rejected because 27 of 35 updates were unsampled and budget saturation itself persists.

The budget-limited-selection account predicts budget/iteration-limited stops. Every sampled update terminates on User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible, or on Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded, and none reaches Solve_Succeeded; 29 of the 35 applied updates reused an initialization plan (selected_iteration 0) while wall time stays ~17.78 s per 0.01 s period with 35 deadline misses. This is the better-supported of the two checked accounts. The 'coordinated with reduced horizon' clause is only partially met because full-horizon sampled updates also stop on budget, so this is retention of the mechanism, not of an exact horizon coupling.

Sampled holding speed remains about 59x the 0.02 m/s limit and the single weight increase is sealed as a physical_tradeoff. The new controller-update (plans) evidence adds nothing that restores an unpenalized holding tip-speed term to adequacy, so the term stays a weakened explanation.

This check produced controller-update (plans) evidence only; no per-tendon force-limit saturation reading was added and both runs record force_bound_violation_n = 0.0. The tension-limit account remains untested rather than refuted.
Terminal reach still passes (terminal_error_m inside the 0.01 m tolerance) and the recorded failure is in holding, not terminal reach; nothing in the new result changes that.

One paired weight change plus a bounded, partially sampled controller-update query cannot establish a dominant cause of the reach/holding outcome; the claim that a single execution does not certify a cause is unchanged.

Causality remains uncertified and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-identification capability is available (unsupported causal_identification), so the deferral still governs. Recommendation acceptance is reported separately from candidate selection.

Do not select improvement-96f0ade35119 as an overall improvement: the sealed comparison is a physical_tradeoff and joint_reach_holding_passed stays false. This candidate disposition is kept separate from the diagnostic recommendation dispositions above.

arguments.expected_observations_interpretation: The proposal listed four expected observations. For solver.terminal_horizon_truncation the retain observation ('effective_horizon below the configured 10 at most sampled updates') is not met - only 2 of 8 sampled updates are below 10; the weaken observation ('equals 10 at all but at most one update') is nearly met (6 of 8 equal 10, with reductions occurring only at the two latest sampled updates), so the truncation account is weakened, not retained. For controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection the retain observation ('budget/iteration-limited stop at most sampled updates') is met at all 8 sampled updates, though the 'coordinated with reduced effective_horizon' clause holds only at updates 30 and 34; the weaken observation ('Solve_Succeeded with full effective_horizon 10') is not observed at any sampled update. These observations therefore leave the saturated-budget account as the better-supported mechanism, as the proposal anticipated, and the two hypotheses are separable by exactly the horizon/status pattern the check recorded.

new_facts.statement: For candidate execution 087adee8e8a24fe88e5c85fe89e638c8 the selected plans view (updates 0,5,10,15,20,25,30,34) records per-update effective_horizon = 10 control intervals at sampled updates 5 (F651), 10 (F469) and 20 (F686), and reduced values only at the two latest sampled updates: 5 at update 30 (F658) and 1 at update 34 (F691). With a 0.01 s control period (F219) and 0.35 s simulated duration (F348) these reductions equal the remaining task time in control intervals (0.05 s -> 5; 0.01 s -> 1), i.e. a receding-horizon-to-terminal effect rather than persistent truncation.

In the same sampled plans view optimization_raw_status is a budget/iteration-limited stop at every sampled update and never a converged solve: update 5 (F673), update 15 (F710) and update 30 (F661) record User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible (F675, F713, F647, F659), and the candidate stopping counts User_Requested_Stop = 34 (F681) plus Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded = 1 (F697) sum to the 35 applied control updates (F426, F518).

Applied control updates are distinct from optimized selections in the sampled view: optimization_selected_iteration is 0 at update 0 (F655), the run records initialization_selected = 29 (F671, F680) with noninitialization_selected = 6 (F715), while the late sampled updates 30 and 34 record selected_iteration 39 (F648) and 68 (F704); most applied control updates therefore reused an initialization plan under a spent budget.

Computation wall time stays far above the simulated step: mean_update_s = 17.77877309145406 s (F703) against a 0.01 s control period (F219) with deadline_misses = 35 (F464, F511), consistent with a saturated solve budget; wall overruns do not imply skipped simulated steps or injected actuator delay.

new_limitations: This revision rests on controller-update (plans) evidence only; no backend motion view and no prediction view were read, so measured trajectory differences and projected-versus-measured agreement are not addressed.
At most 8 of 35 controller updates are shown per query; the unsampled 27 are declared unavailable, not absent, and no pattern is asserted between sampled updates.
arguments.rationale: The check was designed to separate two hypotheses that predict the same recorded holding failure, using only the per-update effective_horizon / optimization_raw_status signature. The returned plans view shows full 10-interval horizons at six of eight sampled updates, with reductions only at the two latest sampled updates that equal the remaining task time in control intervals, and budget/iteration-limited stops at all eight sampled updates with none converged. That refutes persistent budget truncation of the horizon (weakening solver.terminal_horizon_truncation) and supports budget-limited plan selection (retaining controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection). Applied control updates (35) are kept separate from optimized selections (29 initialization-selected, 6 newly optimized) and simulated steps (0.01 s) from wall deadline misses (35, mean 17.78 s): the saturation is in the solve/wall budget, not in skipped simulated steps. Termination by User_Requested_Stop / Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded is kept separate from convergence, and terminal reach (passing) separate from holding (failing); no causality is inferred from citation validity. Recommendation dispositions are reported separately from the controller-candidate decision.
arguments.recommendation: Adopt controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection (budget-limited plan selection) as the better-supported of the two checked accounts; weaken solver.terminal_horizon_truncation, since the sampled effective_horizon follows the remaining task time rather than showing persistent sub-10 truncation. Separately, and independently of this diagnostic acceptance, do not select candidate improvement-96f0ade35119 as an overall improvement (sealed physical_tradeoff; joint reach/holding false). Keep rec-defer-causal-replay and rec-defer-candidate-selection in force and assert no parameter value.
remaining_uncertainty: Only 8 of the 35 controller updates were sampled; per-update effective_horizon and optimization_raw_status for the other 27 are unavailable (not absent), so persistence of any pattern between sampled updates is unverified.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-identification capability exists (unsupported causal_identification), so neither checked account can be upgraded to a certified cause of the holding-speed failure.

Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent; full_snapshots_available false), so per-update cost contributions under the altered weight cannot be quantified.
Whether the late horizon reductions at updates 30 and 34 also occur at unsampled late updates, and whether early horizon values are always exactly 10, is unverified for the 27 unsampled updates.
The exact contribution of budget-limited plan selection to the persistent holding-speed violation remains unattributed; a budget-limited but otherwise adequate plan cannot be excluded.
resolving_evidence: A full-coverage read of effective_horizon and optimization_raw_status for all 35 controller updates (varying update_ids so the unread 27 are covered) to confirm whether full-10 horizons and budget-limited stops are universal.
Retained optimizer iteration traces / full warm plans (currently not retained as control_snapshots.json) to quantify per-update progress with and without the holding tip-speed term.
A closed-loop counterfactual replay capability (currently capability_unavailable) to attribute the holding-speed violation to budget-truncated plan selection versus horizon effects.

A matched read of the backend motion view (measured world-tip position/velocity) and the projected one-step predictions over the full run, to place the sampled holding window in the measured trajectory.
arguments.result_interpretation: The selected evidence query returned the plans view for controller updates 0,5,10,15,20,25,30,34 (8 of 35 updates; the remaining 27 were not sampled, hence unavailable rather than absent). Recorded per-update effective_horizon is 10 control intervals at sampled updates 5,10 and 20 (F651, F469, F686) and reduced only at update 30 (5, F658) and update 34 (1, F691); both reductions equal the remaining task time in control intervals (0.35 s duration F348 minus 0.30 s -> 0.05 s -> 5; minus 0.34 s -> 0.01 s -> 1), so the sampled horizon pattern is the controller receding toward the terminal, not persistent budget truncation. Optimizer termination is budget/iteration-limited at every sampled update: User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible at updates 5,10,15,25,30 (F673, F710, F661; F675, F713, F647, F659) and Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded at update 34, with candidate stopping counts User_Requested_Stop = 34 (F681) and Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded = 1 (F697) summing to the 35 applied updates (F426, F518) - no Solve_Succeeded. Plan selection separates applied updates from optimized selections: initialization_selected = 29 (F671, F680) with only 6 newly optimized (F715), selected_iteration 0 at update 0 (F655) and 39/68 at updates 30/34 (F648, F704). This is controller-update (plans) evidence only, not backend motion: no measured world-tip trajectory or projected one-step prediction was part of this view, so nothing here speaks to the measured holding-speed trace itself.
